name: Data Science & Analytics
tagline: Turn raw data into insights, forecasts and decisions that move a business.

overview.summary: Data scientists and analysts collect, clean and analyse data to answer questions like 'Why did sales drop?', 'Which customers will leave?' or 'What should we stock next month?'. Analysts focus on SQL, dashboards and clear business storytelling; data scientists add statistics, experiments (A/B tests) and predictive models. Both roles exist in almost every industry — banking, telecom, e-commerce, health, garments, NGOs and government.
whyTrending: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects data scientist jobs to grow 35% from 2025 to 2035 — one of the fastest rates of any occupation.
Big data specialists top the WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025 list of fastest-growing jobs.

AI tools made analysis faster, so companies now expect analysts to answer more questions, automate reporting and work with AI-generated insights — raising demand for people who can judge whether the numbers are right.
In Bangladesh, telecom operators, MFS providers (bKash, Nagad), banks and e-commerce firms run data teams for churn, credit and fraud analytics.

roles.title: Data Analyst
roles.description: Writes SQL, builds dashboards and reports, and explains trends to business teams.

roles.title: Data Scientist
roles.description: Uses statistics and machine learning to predict outcomes, segment customers and design experiments.

roles.title: Business Intelligence (BI) Developer
roles.description: Builds the data models and dashboards (Power BI, Tableau, Looker) that managers use every day.

roles.title: Product Analyst
roles.description: Measures how people use an app or website, runs A/B tests and recommends product changes.

roles.title: Analytics Engineer
roles.description: Transforms raw warehouse data into clean, tested, documented tables using tools like dbt.

roles.title: Decision Scientist / Quant Analyst
roles.description: Applies causal inference, forecasting and optimisation to pricing, supply chain or risk decisions.

beginner: Excel / Google Sheets: formulas, pivot tables, charts
SQL: SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, JOIN
Descriptive statistics: mean, median, variance, distributions
Data cleaning: missing values, duplicates, types
Clear charts and storytelling with data
intermediate: Advanced SQL: window functions, CTEs, query optimisation
Power BI or Tableau dashboards with data models
advanced: Causal inference and experiment design at scale
Customer segmentation, churn and lifetime-value modelling
Using LLMs for text analytics and automated insights

stack.note: SQL is the single most requested skill in analytics listings, followed by Python and one BI tool (Power BI is especially common in Bangladesh and South Asia).

roadmap.title: Python and dashboards
goals: Learn pandas for cleaning and analysis
Build an interactive Power BI or Tableau Public dashboard
Learn window functions and CTEs in SQL
Run and interpret a simple A/B test
Publish your work on GitHub and Tableau Public / Power BI gallery

roadmap.title: Modelling and storytelling
goals: Train a churn or sales-forecast model with scikit-learn
Explain model results with feature importance
Learn the basics of dbt or a cloud warehouse
Present one project as a 5-slide business story

interview.question: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING?
interview.answer: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY, usually on aggregated values.

interview.question: Explain a p-value in plain language.
interview.answer: The probability of seeing results at least as extreme as yours if there were really no effect. A small p-value suggests the observed difference is unlikely to be pure chance.

interview.question: How would you design an A/B test?
interview.answer: Define one primary metric and hypothesis, compute required sample size, randomise users, run for a full business cycle, avoid peeking, then check significance and practical impact.

interview.question: What is a window function?
interview.answer: A SQL function that computes a value across related rows without collapsing them — e.g. ROW_NUMBER, running totals or moving averages using OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...).

interview.question: How do you handle missing data?
interview.answer: First understand why it's missing. Then drop, impute (mean/median/model-based), or flag it, depending on the amount and whether the missingness is random.

interview.question: Correlation vs causation?
interview.answer: Correlation means two variables move together; causation means one changes the other. Experiments or causal methods are needed to claim causation.

interview.question: How would you explain a model to a non-technical manager?
interview.answer: Focus on the decision it supports, how accurate it is in business terms, the top drivers, and its limits — avoid jargon and show examples.

interview.question: What is overfitting and how do you detect it?
interview.answer: When a model memorises training data and fails on new data. Detect it with a large gap between training and validation scores; fix with simpler models, regularisation or more data.

interview.question: Which chart would you use to show change over time?
interview.answer: A line chart for continuous time series; a bar chart for a few discrete periods. Avoid pie charts for trends.

interview.question: Revenue dropped 10% last week. How do you investigate?
interview.answer: Check data quality first, then break the metric down by segment (region, channel, product, new vs returning), compare to seasonality, and look for product, pricing or external changes.

remote.note: Estimate. Arc reports an average of $42,875 per year for Bangladesh-based remote data scientists; remote analyst roles usually pay less, senior data scientists more.

sources.label: Arc — Remote software engineer salaries in Bangladesh

global.note: Data analysts typically earn less than data scientists; product and decision scientists at tech firms often earn more.

demandNotes.bangladesh: High for data analysts and BI roles in telecom, banking, MFS, e-commerce, pharma and development organisations. Power BI + SQL is the most common combination in local postings.
demandNotes.remote: High but competitive. Analysts with strong English communication, SQL and a domain specialty (e-commerce, marketing, finance) win remote contracts most easily.
demandNotes.global: Very high. BLS projects 35% growth for data scientists, about 24,800 openings per year in the US alone.

startToday: Complete the first two SQLBolt lessons (about 30 minutes)
Download Power BI Desktop (free) or create a Tableau Public account
Find one dataset you care about on Kaggle or data.worldbank.org
Write down three questions you want to answer with that dataset
Create a GitHub repository for your analytics portfolio
Follow a daily SQL practice habit: one problem per day
